---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m2p4t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, CapLevels, ShedAmounts

VARIABLES phase, ballots, shed, cap, proposal
\* phase: coordinator stage; ballots: each feeder's vote; shed: committed
\* shed total; cap: runtime-adjustable capacity; proposal: amount in play.

vars == <<phase, ballots, shed, cap, proposal>>

MaxCap == 6

Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ ballots \in [Feeders -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ shed \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ cap \in CapLevels
    /\ proposal \in ShedAmounts

AllYes == \A f \in Feeders : ballots[f] = "yes"
SomeNo == \E f \in Feeders : ballots[f] = "no"

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ ballots = [f \in Feeders |-> "none"]
    /\ shed = 0
    /\ cap \in CapLevels
    /\ proposal = 0

\* Coordinator opens a two-phase commit to shed an extra block of load.
OpenRound(a) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ a \in ShedAmounts
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ proposal' = a
    /\ ballots' = [f \in Feeders |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, cap>>

\* A feeder acknowledges it can carry the reduction.
VoteYes(f) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ballots[f] = "none"
    /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![f] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, shed, cap, proposal>>

\* A feeder refuses (already at its floor).
VoteNo(f) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ballots[f] = "none"
    /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![f] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, shed, cap, proposal>>

\* Commit only when unanimous AND the new total stays within capacity.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ AllYes
    /\ shed + proposal <= cap
    /\ shed' = shed + proposal
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballots, cap, proposal>>

\* A round aborts on any refusal, or when a unanimous yes cannot fit the cap.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \/ SomeNo
       \/ (AllYes /\ shed + proposal > cap)
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballots, shed, cap, proposal>>

\* Operators may retune capacity, but never below what is already shed.
Retune ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "committed", "aborted"}
    /\ \E c \in CapLevels :
        /\ c >= shed
        /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballots, shed, proposal>>

\* Close the transaction and return to idle for the next round.
Recycle ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = 0
    /\ ballots' = [f \in Feeders |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in ShedAmounts : OpenRound(a)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : VoteYes(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : VoteNo(f)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Retune
    \/ Recycle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The committed shed load never exceeds the capacity currently in force.
CapNeverExceeded == shed <= cap
=============================================================================
nl:
A regional power-grid load shedder coordinates a small set of distribution feeders to reduce demand during a supply shortfall. Because switching a feeder is disruptive, every additional block of shed load is negotiated with a two-phase commit: the coordinator opens a round proposing an extra amount to shed, each feeder votes yes (it can carry the reduction) or no (it is already at its floor), and the round commits only if every feeder votes yes. When it commits, the proposed amount is added to the total load being shed. If any feeder refuses, the round aborts and nothing changes; a round also aborts when everyone agreed but the proposed total would exceed the capacity in force. Grid operators may retune the overall shed capacity at runtime as the emergency evolves, but the control room policy forbids setting capacity below the load already being shed. After a round commits or aborts, the coordinator recycles back to idle to negotiate the next block.

The actions are: open a shed round with a proposed amount, a feeder votes yes, a feeder votes no, commit an unanimous round (guarded so the new total stays within capacity), abort a round that has a refusal or whose unanimous total would exceed capacity, retune the capacity to any level not below the current shed total, and recycle a finished round back to idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total load being shed never exceeds the shed capacity currently in force.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m7p3t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Patrons, Books

VARIABLES holder, ver, reading, snap
\* holder: current confirmed reservation per book; ver: per-book version
\* stamp; reading: book a patron is mid-reserving; snap: version it observed.

vars == <<holder, ver, reading, snap>>

None == "none"
MaxVer == 4

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in [Books -> Patrons \cup {None}]
    /\ ver \in [Books -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ reading \in [Patrons -> Books \cup {None}]
    /\ snap \in [Patrons -> 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ holder = [b \in Books |-> None]
    /\ ver = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ reading = [p \in Patrons |-> None]
    /\ snap = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]

\* A patron opens a compare-and-swap by reading a free book's version.
StartRead(p, b) ==
    /\ reading[p] = None
    /\ holder[b] = None
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = b]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = ver[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ver>>

\* The swap succeeds only if the version is unchanged; it then bumps ver.
Confirm(p) ==
    /\ reading[p] # None
    /\ LET b == reading[p] IN
        /\ holder[b] = None
        /\ ver[b] = snap[p]
        /\ ver[b] < MaxVer
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = p]
        /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = ver[b] + 1]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* A stale read (someone else moved the version) is rejected.
Reject(p) ==
    /\ reading[p] # None
    /\ ver[reading[p]] # snap[p]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ver, snap>>

\* A slow patron may abandon an outstanding read without failing.
Abandon(p) ==
    /\ reading[p] # None
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ver, snap>>

\* Returning a book frees it and advances the version.
Return(p, b) ==
    /\ holder[b] = p
    /\ ver[b] < MaxVer
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = None]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = ver[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : StartRead(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Confirm(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Reject(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Abandon(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Return(p, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Any patron still holding a read on a now-reserved book is provably stale,
\* so it can never confirm a second reservation on that same book.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A p \in Patrons :
        (reading[p] # None /\ holder[reading[p]] # None)
            => snap[p] < ver[reading[p]]
=============================================================================
nl:
A library book reservation system lets patrons reserve a small collection of high-demand books. Because many patrons compete for the same title, each reservation is made with a compare-and-swap on a per-book version stamp. A patron opens an attempt by reading a currently free book and remembering the version it saw. To confirm, the patron performs the swap: it succeeds only if the book is still free and its version has not moved since the read, and confirming advances the version stamp. If the version has moved, the read is stale and the attempt is rejected, so the patron must start over. Patrons in this system may be slow but never fail, so a slow patron is allowed to abandon an outstanding read at any time and try again later. Returning a book frees it and again advances the version.

The actions are: start a read on a free book (recording the observed version), confirm a reservation by compare-and-swap when the version is unchanged, reject an attempt whose version has moved, abandon an outstanding read (modelling a slow patron), and return a held book. Confirming and returning both advance the book's version stamp.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a book has become reserved, any patron still holding an earlier read of that book has a strictly older observed version and therefore cannot confirm a second, conflicting reservation on it.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m1p5t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, CapLevels

VARIABLES token, waiting, printed, cap
\* token: ring position holding the print token; waiting: admitted jobs not
\* yet printed; printed: jobs already sent to the press; cap: max in flight.

vars == <<token, waiting, printed, cap>>

NumStations == 3
Stations == 0..(NumStations - 1)
OwnerOf(j) == j % NumStations

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Stations
    /\ waiting \subseteq Jobs
    /\ printed \subseteq Jobs
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* The exclusive-access token is handed to the next station around the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % NumStations
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, printed, cap>>

\* A fresh job is admitted to the spool if room remains and it is not done.
Admit(j) ==
    /\ j \notin waiting
    /\ j \notin printed
    /\ Cardinality(waiting) < cap
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed, cap>>

\* Only the token-holding station may print, and only a waiting job; the job
\* moves from waiting to printed in one step -- printing is irreversible.
Print(j) ==
    /\ j \in waiting
    /\ token = OwnerOf(j)
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {j}
    /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap>>

\* A waiting job may be pulled before printing (owner cancels).
Withdraw(j) ==
    /\ j \in waiting
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed, cap>>

\* The spool's in-flight capacity is retuned at runtime.
Recap ==
    /\ \E c \in CapLevels : cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, waiting, printed>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Admit(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Print(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Withdraw(j)
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A job is never simultaneously waiting to print and already printed; since a
\* printed job is never re-admitted, its irreversible print occurs at most once.
PrintOnce == waiting \cap printed = {}
=============================================================================
nl:
A print shop job spooler drives a single press shared by several intake stations arranged in a ring. Exclusive access to the press is granted by a token that circulates around the ring: only the station currently holding the token may commit a print, and printing is irreversible -- once a job is sent to the press it is done. Jobs are admitted to the spool when there is room; the spool has an in-flight capacity that operators retune at runtime as paper and toner allow. A job may be withdrawn while it is still waiting, but a job that has already printed is never re-admitted. Each job is owned by exactly one station, and a job may be printed only when the token rests at its owning station.

The actions are: pass the token to the next station around the ring, admit a new job when the spool is below capacity and the job is neither waiting nor already printed, print a waiting job (only by its owning station while it holds the token), withdraw a still-waiting job, and retune the in-flight capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No job is ever both waiting to print and already printed, and because a printed job is never admitted again, its irreversible print happens at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m5p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Crews, Amounts

VARIABLES stock, phase, proposal, votes
\* stock: containers stacked at each yard zone; phase: idle/proposing; proposal:
\* the transfer under vote <<from,to,amt>>; votes: each crew's ballot.

vars == <<stock, phase, proposal, votes>>

Zones == {"ship", "apron", "gate"}
Quorum == 2
InitTotal == 3
NoBallot == [from |-> "ship", to |-> "ship", amt |-> 0]

TotalStock == stock["ship"] + stock["apron"] + stock["gate"]

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in [Zones -> 0..InitTotal]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "proposing"}
    /\ proposal \in [from : Zones, to : Zones, amt : 0..3]
    /\ votes \in [Crews -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
    /\ stock = [z \in Zones |-> IF z = "ship" THEN 3 ELSE 0]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ proposal = NoBallot
    /\ votes = [c \in Crews |-> "none"]

YesCount == Cardinality({c \in Crews : votes[c] = "yes"})

\* A crew proposes moving a batch of containers between two zones.
Propose(f, t, a) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ f # t
    /\ a \in Amounts
    /\ stock[f] >= a
    /\ phase' = "proposing"
    /\ proposal' = [from |-> f, to |-> t, amt |-> a]
    /\ votes' = [c \in Crews |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED stock

\* A crew approves the pending crane move.
VoteYes(c) ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ votes[c] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, phase, proposal>>

\* A crew objects (deck congestion, lashing not ready).
VoteNo(c) ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ votes[c] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, phase, proposal>>

\* With a quorum of approvals the move executes as a pure transfer.
Execute ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ YesCount >= Quorum
    /\ stock[proposal.from] >= proposal.amt
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![proposal.from] = @ - proposal.amt,
                              ![proposal.to] = @ + proposal.amt]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = NoBallot
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

\* The proposal is abandoned (a quorum never formed among slow crews).
Abandon ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = NoBallot
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f, t \in Zones, a \in Amounts : Propose(f, t, a)
    \/ \E c \in Crews : VoteYes(c)
    \/ \E c \in Crews : VoteNo(c)
    \/ Execute
    \/ Abandon

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Crane moves only relocate containers, so the yard's total count is invariant.
Conserved == TotalStock = InitTotal
=============================================================================
nl:
A container-ship crane yard relocates containers among three zones -- the ship, the apron, and the gate -- using ship-to-shore cranes. Because a mis-stowed batch is dangerous, every crane move is authorized by quorum voting among the yard crews: a crew proposes moving a batch of a given size from one zone to another, crews vote to approve or object, and the move executes only once a quorum of approvals is reached. Crews may be slow but never fail, so a proposal that never gathers a quorum among slow crews is simply abandoned and the yard returns to idle. A move that executes is a pure transfer: the batch leaves the source zone and arrives at the destination zone, and no containers are created or destroyed anywhere in the yard.

The actions are: propose a batch move between two zones (only if the source holds enough), a crew votes yes, a crew votes no, execute the move once a quorum of yes votes exists (transferring the batch), and abandon a proposal that no quorum approved.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of containers across all three yard zones is always exactly the amount the yard started with, since every crane move only relocates containers and never creates or destroys any.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m9p1t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Controllers

VARIABLES log, record, epoch, snap, alive
\* log: append-only history of writers to the shared plan; record: last writer
\* stamped on the plan; epoch: reconfiguration counter; snap: each controller's
\* observed version; alive: controllers that have not silently crashed.

vars == <<log, record, epoch, snap, alive>>

MaxLen == 2
Recfg == "recfg"
Version == Len(log)

TypeOK ==
    /\ log \in Seq(Controllers \cup {Recfg})
    /\ Len(log) <= MaxLen
    /\ record \in Controllers \cup {Recfg, "none"}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxLen
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxLen]
    /\ alive \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ record = "none"
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ alive = [c \in Controllers |-> TRUE]

\* A live controller reads (or re-reads) the current plan version.
Read(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ snap[c] # Version
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = Version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<log, record, epoch, alive>>

\* A controller commits its update only if no update slipped in since its read;
\* the write is appended to the log and stamped on the record together.
Write(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ snap[c] = Version
    /\ Version < MaxLen
    /\ log' = Append(log, c)
    /\ record' = c
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = Version + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alive>>

\* An epoch reconfiguration is itself a logged write that supersedes readers.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ Version < MaxLen
    /\ epoch < MaxLen
    /\ log' = Append(log, Recfg)
    /\ record' = Recfg
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, alive>>

\* At most one controller may crash silently and take no further part.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ \A d \in Controllers : alive[d]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<log, record, epoch, snap>>

\* Oldest history is garbage-collected once the log is full; the current head
\* (and thus the record it names) is retained.
Trim ==
    /\ Version = MaxLen
    /\ log' = Tail(log)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, epoch, snap, alive>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Read(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Write(c)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)
    \/ Trim

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The shared record always names the head of the append-only history, so no
\* committed update is ever silently dropped from the plan.
NoLostUpdate == Version > 0 => record = log[Version]
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {k1, k2}
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator maintains a single shared runway-assignment plan that several controllers update. To coordinate under changing conditions, the system is organized into numbered epochs: a reconfiguration begins a new epoch and is itself recorded as a write that supersedes any controller still working from the old plan. Each controller reads the current version of the plan before writing, and its update commits only if no other update has landed since that read; committing appends the controller to the plan's append-only history and stamps it as the record's latest writer in the same step. A controller whose read has been overtaken must re-read before it can write again, which prevents it from clobbering an update it never saw. Any single controller may crash silently and simply stops participating, without announcing its departure.

The actions are: a live controller reads or re-reads the current plan version, a live controller writes an update when its read is still current (appending to the history and stamping the record), a reconfiguration opens a new epoch as a logged write, a single controller crashes silently (at most one crash occurs), and the oldest history entry is garbage-collected once the log is full (the current head, which the record names, is kept).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared record always names the most recent entry of the plan's append-only history, so no committed update is ever silently lost.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m9p1t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, CapLevels

VARIABLES version, record, epoch, ack, mirror, cap
\* version: master record version; record: id that wrote the master; epoch:
\* reconfiguration counter; ack: version each robot has synced; mirror: each
\* robot's local copy of the record; cap: runtime write budget per epoch.

vars == <<version, record, epoch, ack, mirror, cap>>

MaxV == 3
MaxE == 2
Init0 == "init"

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxV
    /\ record \in Robots \cup {Init0}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxE
    /\ ack \in [Robots -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ mirror \in [Robots -> Robots \cup {Init0}]
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ record = Init0
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ ack = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ mirror = [r \in Robots |-> Init0]
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* A robot writes the shared inventory record only when it is caught up to the
\* current version, so it cannot overwrite an update it never observed.
Write(r) ==
    /\ ack[r] = version
    /\ version < cap
    /\ version < MaxV
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ record' = r
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![r] = version + 1]
    /\ mirror' = [mirror EXCEPT ![r] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap>>

\* A lagging robot resynchronizes its local mirror to the master record.
Refresh(r) ==
    /\ ack[r] < version
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![r] = version]
    /\ mirror' = [mirror EXCEPT ![r] = record]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, record, epoch, cap>>

\* An epoch reconfiguration renumbers the fleet.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, record, ack, mirror, cap>>

\* The per-epoch write capacity is retuned at runtime.
Recap ==
    /\ \E c \in CapLevels : cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, record, epoch, ack, mirror>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Write(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Refresh(r)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every robot that believes it is current holds a mirror equal to the master
\* record, so no committed update is silently lost from a caught-up replica.
NoLostUpdate == \A r \in Robots : (ack[r] = version) => mirror[r] = record
=============================================================================
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single inventory record that every robot both reads and updates. To keep the record consistent as robots come and go, the system runs in numbered epochs, and each epoch grants a write capacity -- a budget on how many updates may be applied before a reconfiguration is needed. A robot may write the record only when it is caught up to the current version; writing advances the version, stamps the writer's id on the record, updates that robot's local mirror, and marks the robot as caught up in one step. This up-to-date-basis rule is what prevents a robot from clobbering an update it never observed. A robot that has fallen behind resynchronizes by copying the master record into its local mirror and marking itself caught up. An epoch reconfiguration renumbers the fleet, and the per-epoch write capacity is retuned at runtime.

The actions are: a caught-up robot writes the record within the epoch's capacity, a lagging robot resynchronizes its mirror to the master, a reconfiguration advances the epoch, and the write capacity is retuned at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every robot that believes it is up to date holds a local mirror equal to the master record, so no committed update is ever silently lost from a caught-up replica.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m2p1t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, Txns

VARIABLES phase, votes, msgs, posted
\* phase: 2PC stage per settlement txn; votes: each bank's prepare vote per
\* txn; msgs: in-flight apply messages (a bag, consumable in any order);
\* posted: settlements written to the shared ledger.

vars == <<phase, votes, msgs, posted>>

Stages == {"init", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Txns -> Stages]
    /\ votes \in [Txns -> [Banks -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
    /\ msgs \subseteq Txns
    /\ posted \subseteq Txns

Init ==
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "init"]
    /\ votes = [t \in Txns |-> [b \in Banks |-> "none"]]
    /\ msgs = {}
    /\ posted = {}

AllYes(t) == \A b \in Banks : votes[t][b] = "yes"
SomeNo(t) == \E b \in Banks : votes[t][b] = "no"

\* The coordinator opens prepare voting for a settlement.
Open(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "init"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = [b \in Banks |-> "none"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<msgs, posted>>

\* A bank prepares (agrees to settle).
Prepare(t, b) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ votes[t][b] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t][b] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, msgs, posted>>

\* A bank refuses (insufficient funds).
Refuse(t, b) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ votes[t][b] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t][b] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, msgs, posted>>

\* Unanimous prepare commits the txn and emits an apply message.
CommitTxn(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ AllYes(t)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, posted>>

\* Any refusal aborts the txn; nothing is emitted.
AbortTxn(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ SomeNo(t)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, msgs, posted>>

\* Apply messages arrive in any order; applying posts the settlement.
Apply(t) ==
    /\ t \in msgs
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {t}
    /\ posted' = posted \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes>>

\* A finished settlement slot is recycled for reuse.
Recycle(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ t \notin msgs
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "init"]
    /\ posted' = posted \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, msgs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Open(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, b \in Banks : Prepare(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, b \in Banks : Refuse(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : CommitTxn(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : AbortTxn(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Apply(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Recycle(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed settlement is accounted for -- either its apply message is
\* still in flight or it has already been posted -- so no update is ever lost,
\* even when apply messages are delivered out of order.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A t \in Txns : phase[t] = "committed" => (t \in msgs \/ t \in posted)
=============================================================================
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch posts a set of settlement transactions to a shared ledger using two-phase commit across the participating banks. For each transaction the coordinator opens a prepare vote; each bank prepares (agrees to settle) or refuses (insufficient funds). A transaction that is unanimously prepared commits and emits an apply message; a transaction with any refusal aborts and emits nothing. Apply messages travel over a network where messages can be reordered, so they may be delivered and processed in any order; processing an apply message posts that settlement to the shared ledger. A finished transaction slot, once its apply message is no longer in flight, is recycled so the slot can be reused for another settlement.

The actions are: open prepare voting for a transaction, a bank prepares, a bank refuses, commit a unanimously-prepared transaction (emitting an apply message), abort a transaction that has a refusal, apply an in-flight message in any order (posting the settlement), and recycle a finished slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed settlement is always accounted for -- either its apply message is still in flight or it has already been posted to the ledger -- so no committed update is ever lost, even when apply messages arrive out of order.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m6p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Calls, CapLevels

VARIABLES owner, expiry, served, clock, cap
\* owner: car leasing each hall call; expiry: lease deadline per call; served:
\* calls whose car has been irreversibly dispatched; clock: discrete time;
\* cap: max concurrent leases, retuned at runtime.

vars == <<owner, expiry, served, clock, cap>>

None == "none"
MaxT == 3

Leased == {c \in Calls : owner[c] # None}

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Calls -> Cars \cup {None}]
    /\ expiry \in [Calls -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ served \subseteq Calls
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ owner = [c \in Calls |-> None]
    /\ expiry = [c \in Calls |-> 0]
    /\ served = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* A car takes a time-limited lease on an unserved hall call.
Acquire(e, c) ==
    /\ owner[c] = None
    /\ c \notin served
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ Cardinality(Leased) < cap
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = e]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![c] = clock + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, clock, cap>>

\* The lease-holder irreversibly dispatches its car to the call, retiring the
\* call: the lease is released and the call is marked served in one step.
Serve(e, c) ==
    /\ owner[c] = e
    /\ expiry[c] > clock
    /\ c \notin served
    /\ served' = served \cup {c}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, clock, cap>>

\* An expired lease is reclaimed so another car may bid.
Expire(c) ==
    /\ owner[c] # None
    /\ expiry[c] <= clock
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, served, clock, cap>>

\* Time advances.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, expiry, served, cap>>

\* The concurrent-lease capacity is retuned at runtime.
Recap ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels : cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, expiry, served, clock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Cars, c \in Calls : Acquire(e, c)
    \/ \E e \in Cars, c \in Calls : Serve(e, c)
    \/ \E c \in Calls : Expire(c)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Once a call has been dispatched it is retired: it holds no lease and can
\* never be leased again, so its irreversible dispatch happens at most once.
AtMostOnce == \A c \in Calls : c \in served => owner[c] = None
=============================================================================
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper dispatches cars to hall calls using lease-based ownership with expiry. Before a car may serve a hall call, it acquires a time-limited lease on that call, and only a bounded number of leases may be held at once; that concurrency capacity is retuned at runtime as traffic shifts. The lease-holding car then irreversibly dispatches itself to the call: dispatching is a committed action, so in the same step the call is marked served and its lease is released, retiring the call permanently -- a served call can never be leased again. If a lease expires before the car dispatches, the lease is reclaimed and another car may bid. A global clock advances in discrete ticks, and a lease is valid only while the clock is still before its deadline.

The actions are: acquire a lease on an unserved call while under the concurrency capacity and before the deadline horizon, irreversibly dispatch the leased car (marking the call served and releasing the lease), reclaim an expired lease, advance the clock by one tick, and retune the concurrency capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a hall call has been dispatched it is retired -- it holds no lease and can never be leased again -- so its irreversible dispatch happens at most once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m8p2t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Homes, Doors

VARIABLES pool, held, level, door
\* pool: free actuator tokens in the shared pool; held: tokens each home holds;
\* level: lock level each home has taken (idle/coarse/fine); door: the fine-
\* locked door per home. Two independent homes draw from the one token pool.

vars == <<pool, held, level, door>>

Total == 3
None == "none"

RECURSIVE SumHeld(_)
SumHeld(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET h == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN held[h] + SumHeld(S \ {h})

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ held \in [Homes -> 0..Total]
    /\ level \in [Homes -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}]
    /\ door \in [Homes -> Doors \cup {None}]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ held = [h \in Homes |-> 0]
    /\ level = [h \in Homes |-> "idle"]
    /\ door = [h \in Homes |-> None]

\* Take the coarse (whole-home) lock first.
LockCoarse(h) ==
    /\ level[h] = "idle"
    /\ level' = [level EXCEPT ![h] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, door>>

\* Then take a fine lock on a specific door not held finely by the other home.
LockFine(h, d) ==
    /\ level[h] = "coarse"
    /\ \A g \in Homes : g # h => door[g] # d
    /\ level' = [level EXCEPT ![h] = "fine"]
    /\ door' = [door EXCEPT ![h] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held>>

\* Under the fine lock, draw one actuator token from the shared pool.
Grab(h) ==
    /\ level[h] = "fine"
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ held[h] < Total
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![h] = held[h] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, door>>

\* Return one token to the shared pool.
Release(h) ==
    /\ level[h] = "fine"
    /\ held[h] > 0
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![h] = held[h] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, door>>

\* Drop the fine lock.
UnlockFine(h) ==
    /\ level[h] = "fine"
    /\ level' = [level EXCEPT ![h] = "coarse"]
    /\ door' = [door EXCEPT ![h] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held>>

\* Drop the coarse lock.
UnlockCoarse(h) ==
    /\ level[h] = "coarse"
    /\ level' = [level EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, door>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Homes : LockCoarse(h)
    \/ \E h \in Homes, d \in Doors : LockFine(h, d)
    \/ \E h \in Homes : Grab(h)
    \/ \E h \in Homes : Release(h)
    \/ \E h \in Homes : UnlockFine(h)
    \/ \E h \in Homes : UnlockCoarse(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Tokens are only ever moved between the shared pool and the homes, never
\* created or destroyed, so the grand total is invariant.
Conserved == pool + SumHeld(Homes) = Total
=============================================================================
nl:
A smart-home door lock network serves two independent homes that share a single pool of actuator tokens; a token is what physically drives a lock, and there are only so many to go around. Each home coordinates its own doors with hierarchical locks: it must take a coarse whole-home lock before it can take a fine lock on a specific door, and a fine lock on a door is exclusive across the two homes. Only while holding a fine lock may a home draw an actuator token from the shared pool to operate a door, and it later returns the token to the pool. Every draw removes exactly one token from the pool and adds it to the home, and every return does the reverse, so tokens only ever move between the pool and the homes. A home unwinds its locks in reverse order: drop the fine lock, then the coarse lock.

The actions are: take the coarse lock, take a fine lock on a free door, draw one token from the shared pool while fine-locked, return one token to the pool, drop the fine lock, and drop the coarse lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of actuator tokens -- those free in the shared pool plus those held by the two homes -- is always exactly the pool's starting total, since tokens are only moved and never created or destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m6p5t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, Settlements

VARIABLES lease, gen, finalized, inbox
\* lease: bank leasing the right to finalize each settlement; gen: lease
\* generation per settlement; finalized: settlements irreversibly finalized;
\* inbox: in-flight finalize messages (a bag) each stamped with a generation.

vars == <<lease, gen, finalized, inbox>>

None == "none"
MaxGen == 1
Msgs == [sid : Settlements, ep : 0..MaxGen]

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Settlements -> Banks \cup {None}]
    /\ gen \in [Settlements -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ finalized \subseteq Settlements
    /\ inbox \subseteq Msgs

Init ==
    /\ lease = [s \in Settlements |-> None]
    /\ gen = [s \in Settlements |-> 0]
    /\ finalized = {}
    /\ inbox = {}

\* A bank leases the right to finalize an unfinalized settlement, bumping the
\* lease generation.
Claim(b, s) ==
    /\ lease[s] = None
    /\ s \notin finalized
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = gen[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, inbox>>

\* The lease-holder emits a finalize message stamped with the current gen.
Emit(s) ==
    /\ lease[s] # None
    /\ [sid |-> s, ep |-> gen[s]] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[sid |-> s, ep |-> gen[s]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, gen, finalized>>

\* The lease may expire (nondeterministic timeout), releasing ownership.
Expire(s) ==
    /\ lease[s] # None
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, finalized, inbox>>

\* Messages arrive in any order; a message finalizes only if its stamp still
\* matches the live lease generation. Finalizing is irreversible.
Finalize(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ lease[m.sid] # None
    /\ m.ep = gen[m.sid]
    /\ m.sid \notin finalized
    /\ finalized' = finalized \cup {m.sid}
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![m.sid] = None]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED gen

\* A reordered message whose stamp is stale is discarded.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ep # gen[m.sid]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, gen, finalized>>

\* A settlement slot is recycled: reopen a finalized one, or reset an exhausted
\* idle one, so the model keeps making progress.
Recycle(s) ==
    /\ \/ s \in finalized
       \/ (lease[s] = None /\ gen[s] = MaxGen)
    /\ finalized' = finalized \ {s}
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, inbox>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Settlements : Claim(b, s)
    \/ \E s \in Settlements : Emit(s)
    \/ \E s \in Settlements : Expire(s)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Finalize(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropStale(m)
    \/ \E s \in Settlements : Recycle(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A finalized settlement holds no live lease and has no message still pending,
\* so its irreversible finalization can never be applied a second time.
AtMostOnce ==
    \A s \in Settlements :
        s \in finalized => (lease[s] = None /\ [sid |-> s, ep |-> gen[s]] \notin inbox)
=============================================================================
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch finalizes settlements using lease-based ownership with expiry over an unreliable network where messages can be reordered. To finalize a settlement, a bank first leases the exclusive right to finalize it; each lease is stamped with a fresh generation number. The lease-holder emits a finalize message carrying that generation. Because the network reorders messages, finalize messages may be delivered in any order and at any time. A message finalizes its settlement only if its stamped generation still matches the settlement's live lease generation; finalizing is irreversible and releases the lease. A lease may expire nondeterministically at any time, releasing ownership; a reordered message whose stamp no longer matches the live generation is simply discarded as stale. Settlement slots are recycled -- a finalized one may be reopened, and an exhausted idle one reset -- so processing continues.

The actions are: lease the right to finalize an unfinalized settlement (bumping its generation), emit a generation-stamped finalize message, let a lease expire, finalize a settlement from a matching in-flight message in any order, discard a stale reordered message, and recycle a settlement slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A finalized settlement holds no live lease and has no matching finalize message still pending, so its irreversible finalization can never be applied a second time even when messages arrive out of order.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m5p1t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Writers, Replicas

VARIABLES ver, val, phase, base, acks, rver
\* ver/val: committed version and value of the shared catalog record; phase:
\* idle or collecting; base: version the active proposal read; acks: which
\* replicas have acked it; rver: version each replica has applied.

vars == <<ver, val, phase, base, acks, rver>>

MaxV == 2
Quorum == 2
Init0 == "init"

AckCount == Cardinality({r \in Replicas : acks[r]})

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ val \in Writers \cup {Init0}
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "collecting"}
    /\ base \in 0..MaxV
    /\ acks \in [Replicas -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ rver \in [Replicas -> 0..MaxV]

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ val = Init0
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ base = 0
    /\ acks = [r \in Replicas |-> FALSE]
    /\ rver = [r \in Replicas |-> 0]

\* A writer opens a quorum write, reading the current version as its basis.
Propose(w) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ phase' = "collecting"
    /\ base' = ver
    /\ acks' = [r \in Replicas |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, val, rver>>

\* A replica acks only if it has seen at least the proposal's basis version;
\* slow replicas may simply never ack, and a quorum forms without them.
Ack(r) ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ ~acks[r]
    /\ rver[r] >= base
    /\ acks' = [acks EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, val, phase, base, rver>>

\* The write commits only with a quorum and only if the basis is still current
\* (nobody else committed since the read), so no update is silently lost.
Commit(w) ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ AckCount >= Quorum
    /\ base = ver
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ val' = w
    /\ rver' = [r \in Replicas |-> IF acks[r] THEN ver + 1 ELSE rver[r]]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<base, acks>>

\* The proposal is abandoned (no quorum among slow replicas, or basis stale).
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, val, base, acks, rver>>

\* A lagging replica catches up to the committed version.
Sync(r) ==
    /\ rver[r] < ver
    /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![r] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, val, phase, base, acks>>

\* When the version horizon is reached, the catalog is archived and restarted.
Reset ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ val' = Init0
    /\ base' = 0
    /\ rver' = [r \in Replicas |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, acks>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Propose(w)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas : Ack(r)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Commit(w)
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E r \in Replicas : Sync(r)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every replica that has acked the active proposal had already seen its basis
\* version, so the quorum that commits builds on witnessed state and no update
\* is lost by a write from a replica that lagged behind.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A r \in Replicas : (phase = "collecting" /\ acks[r]) => rver[r] >= base
=============================================================================
nl:
A library book reservation system keeps a shared catalog record replicated across several branch replicas, and every update to the record is committed by quorum voting. A writer opens an update by reading the record's current version as its basis. Each replica may then ack the proposal, but only if it has already seen at least the basis version; replicas may be slow but never fail, so a slow replica might simply never ack, and a quorum still forms from the others. The write commits only when a quorum has acked and the basis is still the current committed version -- meaning no other update slipped in since the read -- and committing advances the version, stamps the new value, and brings the acking replicas up to the new version. If a quorum never forms or the basis has gone stale, the proposal is abandoned. A lagging replica may independently catch up to the committed version; when the version horizon is reached, the catalog is archived and restarted.

The actions are: propose a quorum write (reading the current version as basis), a replica acks if it has seen the basis, commit with a quorum when the basis is still current, abandon a proposal, let a lagging replica catch up, and archive-and-restart the catalog at the version horizon.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every replica that acks the active proposal has already seen its basis version, so the quorum that commits builds only on witnessed state and no update is ever lost to a write from a replica that had lagged behind.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m2p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Parties, Tasks, CapLevels

VARIABLES phase, votes, executed, cap
\* phase: 2PC stage per pick task; votes: each party's prepare vote per task;
\* executed: tasks whose irreversible physical pick has happened; cap: max
\* concurrently active tasks, retuned at runtime.

vars == <<phase, votes, executed, cap>>

Stages == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}
Active == {t \in Tasks : phase[t] \in {"voting", "committed"}}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Tasks -> Stages]
    /\ votes \in [Tasks -> [Parties -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
    /\ executed \subseteq Tasks
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ phase = [t \in Tasks |-> "idle"]
    /\ votes = [t \in Tasks |-> [p \in Parties |-> "none"]]
    /\ executed = {}
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

AllYes(t) == \A p \in Parties : votes[t][p] = "yes"
SomeNo(t) == \E p \in Parties : votes[t][p] = "no"

\* Open a two-phase commit for a pick, subject to the active-task capacity.
Open(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "idle"
    /\ t \notin executed
    /\ Cardinality(Active) < cap
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = [p \in Parties |-> "none"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<executed, cap>>

\* A party votes to prepare the pick.
PrepareYes(t, p) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ votes[t][p] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t][p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, executed, cap>>

\* A party refuses (item missing or arm busy).
PrepareNo(t, p) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ votes[t][p] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t][p] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, executed, cap>>

\* Unanimous prepare commits the decision (not yet the physical pick).
CommitDecision(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ AllYes(t)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, executed, cap>>

\* Any refusal aborts.
AbortDecision(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "voting"
    /\ SomeNo(t)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, executed, cap>>

\* The committed pick is physically executed exactly once -- irreversible.
Execute(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "committed"
    /\ t \notin executed
    /\ executed' = executed \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, cap>>

\* A completed pick is cleared, dropping its executed mark and freeing the slot.
Clear(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "committed"
    /\ t \in executed
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ executed' = executed \ {t}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = [p \in Parties |-> "none"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED cap

\* An aborted task returns to idle.
Reopen(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "aborted"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, executed, cap>>

\* The active-task capacity is retuned at runtime.
Recap ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels : cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, executed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Open(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks, p \in Parties : PrepareYes(t, p)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks, p \in Parties : PrepareNo(t, p)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : CommitDecision(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : AbortDecision(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Execute(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Clear(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tasks : Reopen(t)
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A task is marked executed only while its decision stands committed; it can
\* never be reopened while executed, so the irreversible pick happens at most once.
AtMostOnce == \A t \in Tasks : t \in executed => phase[t] = "committed"
=============================================================================
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet executes item picks, each coordinated by a two-phase commit between a picking arm and its shelf controller. Because physically removing an item from a shelf is irreversible, the decision to pick is committed first and the physical pick is carried out separately, at most once. A pick task opens for voting subject to a capacity on how many tasks may be active at once, and that capacity is retuned at runtime. Both parties prepare (vote yes) or refuse (vote no); a unanimous prepare commits the decision, while any refusal aborts. Once a task's decision is committed, its physical pick is executed exactly once, and a task can never be reopened while it is still marked executed. A completed pick is later cleared -- dropping its executed mark and freeing its slot -- and an aborted task simply returns to idle.

The actions are: open a task for voting within capacity, a party votes yes, a party votes no, commit the decision on unanimous prepare, abort on any refusal, execute the committed pick once, clear a completed pick, reopen an aborted task, and retune the active-task capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A task is marked executed only while its decision stands committed and can never be reopened while executed, so the irreversible physical pick happens at most once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m5p4t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Blocks, CapLevels

VARIABLES occ, cap, phase, target, votes
\* occ: trains occupying each track block; cap: per-block capacity (retuned at
\* runtime); phase: idle/voting; target: block the pending admit is for; votes:
\* each signal controller's ballot on the pending admit.

vars == <<occ, cap, phase, target, votes>>

MaxOcc == 2
Quorum == 2
YesCount == Cardinality({c \in Controllers : votes[c] = "yes"})

TypeOK ==
    /\ occ \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxOcc]
    /\ cap \in [Blocks -> CapLevels]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ target \in Blocks
    /\ votes \in [Controllers -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ cap \in [Blocks -> CapLevels]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ target \in Blocks
    /\ votes = [c \in Controllers |-> "none"]

\* Signal controllers open a vote to admit a train into a specific block.
Propose(b) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ target' = b
    /\ votes' = [c \in Controllers |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap>>

\* A controller clears the movement.
VoteYes(c) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[c] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap, phase, target>>

\* A controller holds the movement (conflicting route).
VoteNo(c) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[c] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap, phase, target>>

\* With a quorum, admit the train only if the block is below its capacity.
Admit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ YesCount >= Quorum
    /\ occ[target] < cap[target]
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![target] = occ[target] + 1]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, target, votes>>

\* No quorum forms; the movement is held.
Reject ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap, target, votes>>

\* A train departs a block.
Depart(b) ==
    /\ occ[b] > 0
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = occ[b] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, phase, target, votes>>

\* A block's capacity is retuned at runtime, but never below its occupancy.
Recap(b) ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels :
        /\ k >= occ[b]
        /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![b] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, phase, target, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Propose(b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : VoteYes(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : VoteNo(c)
    \/ Admit
    \/ Reject
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Depart(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Recap(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No track block ever holds more trains than its current capacity permits.
BoundedCapacity == \A b \in Blocks : occ[b] <= cap[b]
=============================================================================
nl:
A subway signalling block system controls how many trains may occupy each track block. Admitting a train into a block is authorized by quorum voting among the signal controllers: the controllers open a vote targeting a specific block, each controller either clears the movement or holds it for a conflicting route, and the train is admitted only once a quorum has cleared it. Crucially, an admission is allowed only if the target block is still below its capacity. Each block's capacity is retuned at runtime as maintenance and headway policies change, but a block's capacity is never lowered below the number of trains currently occupying it. Trains also depart blocks, reducing occupancy. If a quorum never forms, the movement is held and the system returns to idle.

The actions are: open a vote to admit a train into a block, a controller clears the movement, a controller holds the movement, admit the train once a quorum clears it and the block is below capacity, hold the movement when no quorum forms, a train departs a block, and retune a block's capacity at runtime to any level not below its current occupancy.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No track block ever holds more trains than its current capacity permits.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m8p4t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Sections, Students

VARIABLES enrolled, coarse, fine, inbox
\* enrolled: seats taken in each section; coarse: registrar-wide lock held?;
\* fine: the one section currently fine-locked (or none); inbox: pending enroll
\* request messages, delivered in any order.

vars == <<enrolled, coarse, fine, inbox>>

Cap == 2
None == "none"
Msgs == [sec : Sections, stu : Students]

TypeOK ==
    /\ enrolled \in [Sections -> 0..Cap]
    /\ coarse \in BOOLEAN
    /\ fine \in Sections \cup {None}
    /\ inbox \subseteq Msgs

Init ==
    /\ enrolled = [s \in Sections |-> 0]
    /\ coarse = FALSE
    /\ fine = None
    /\ inbox = {}

\* A student submits an enroll request; it joins the reorderable message bag.
Request(s, u) ==
    /\ [sec |-> s, stu |-> u] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[sec |-> s, stu |-> u]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, coarse, fine>>

\* Take the coarse registrar-wide lock first.
LockCoarse ==
    /\ ~coarse
    /\ coarse' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, fine, inbox>>

\* Then take the fine lock on a specific section.
LockFine(s) ==
    /\ coarse
    /\ fine = None
    /\ fine' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, coarse, inbox>>

\* Process an enroll message (in any order) only if the fine-locked section is
\* still below capacity -- this is what keeps capacity from being exceeded.
Process(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ fine = m.sec
    /\ enrolled[m.sec] < Cap
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![m.sec] = enrolled[m.sec] + 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

\* A request for a full fine-locked section is rejected.
Reject(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ fine = m.sec
    /\ enrolled[m.sec] = Cap
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, coarse, fine>>

\* Drop the fine lock.
UnlockFine ==
    /\ fine # None
    /\ fine' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, coarse, inbox>>

\* Drop the coarse lock.
UnlockCoarse ==
    /\ coarse
    /\ fine = None
    /\ coarse' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, fine, inbox>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Sections, u \in Students : Request(s, u)
    \/ LockCoarse
    \/ \E s \in Sections : LockFine(s)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Process(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Reject(m)
    \/ UnlockFine
    \/ UnlockCoarse

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No section ever enrolls more students than its seat capacity, even though
\* enroll messages are processed out of order.
BoundedSeats == \A s \in Sections : enrolled[s] <= Cap
=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system enrolls students into sections, each with a fixed seat capacity that must never be exceeded. Enrollment is serialized with hierarchical locks: the registrar takes a coarse registrar-wide lock first, then a fine lock on a specific section, before it may process enrollments for that section. Students submit enroll requests asynchronously, and because requests travel over a network that can reorder messages, they sit in a message bag and are processed in any order. When the registrar processes an enroll message for the section it holds finely locked, it admits the student only if that section is still below capacity; a request for a section that is already full is rejected. The registrar unwinds its locks in reverse order: drop the fine lock, then the coarse lock.

The actions are: a student submits an enroll request into the reorderable bag, take the coarse registrar lock, take a fine lock on a section, process an enroll message in any order when the section is below capacity, reject a message for a full section, drop the fine lock, and drop the coarse lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No section ever enrolls more students than its seat capacity, even though enroll requests are processed out of order.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m7p5t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Wards, Batches

VARIABLES token, sealed, attempt, base
\* token: the shared pool's compare-and-swap control register; sealed: batches
\* irreversibly sealed for issue; attempt: the batch each ward is trying to
\* seal; base: the token value each ward read when it began.

vars == <<token, sealed, attempt, base>>

None == "none"
MaxTok == 3

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in 0..MaxTok
    /\ sealed \subseteq Batches
    /\ attempt \in [Wards -> Batches \cup {None}]
    /\ base \in [Wards -> 0..MaxTok]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ sealed = {}
    /\ attempt = [w \in Wards |-> None]
    /\ base = [w \in Wards |-> 0]

\* A ward begins a seal on an unsealed batch, reading the shared register.
Begin(w, b) ==
    /\ attempt[w] = None
    /\ b \notin sealed
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![w] = b]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![w] = token]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sealed>>

\* The seal commits by compare-and-swap: only if the register is unchanged.
\* Sealing is irreversible, bumps the register, and invalidates every ward's
\* in-flight attempt on that same batch.
Seal(w) ==
    /\ attempt[w] # None
    /\ base[w] = token
    /\ token < MaxTok
    /\ LET b == attempt[w] IN
        /\ b \notin sealed
        /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {b}
        /\ attempt' = [x \in Wards |-> IF attempt[x] = b THEN None ELSE attempt[x]]
    /\ token' = token + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED base

\* A stale compare-and-swap (register moved) is retried from scratch.
Retry(w) ==
    /\ attempt[w] # None
    /\ base[w] # token
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![w] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sealed, base>>

\* A ward abandons its attempt.
Cancel(w) ==
    /\ attempt[w] # None
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![w] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sealed, base>>

\* A sealed batch is issued and its slot recycled, resetting the register.
Recycle(b) ==
    /\ b \in sealed
    /\ sealed' = sealed \ {b}
    /\ token' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempt, base>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Wards, b \in Batches : Begin(w, b)
    \/ \E w \in Wards : Seal(w)
    \/ \E w \in Wards : Retry(w)
    \/ \E w \in Wards : Cancel(w)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Recycle(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Once a batch has been sealed, no ward is still attempting to seal it, so its
\* irreversible seal can never be applied a second time.
SealedOnce == \A b \in Batches : b \in sealed => \A w \in Wards : attempt[w] # b
=============================================================================
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker serves two independent hospital wards that share one pool of blood batches. Sealing a batch for issue is irreversible -- once sealed it is committed to a patient -- so each batch must be sealed at most once. Wards coordinate through a single shared compare-and-swap control register on the pool. A ward begins a seal by choosing an unsealed batch and reading the register's current value. It commits the seal by compare-and-swap: the seal succeeds only if the register has not changed since the read. A successful seal is irreversible, advances the register, and in the same step invalidates every ward's in-flight attempt on that same batch, so no other ward can also seal it. If the register has moved, the ward's attempt is stale and is retried from scratch; a ward may also simply abandon its attempt. A sealed batch is eventually issued and its slot recycled, which resets the shared register.

The actions are: begin a seal on an unsealed batch (reading the register), commit the seal by compare-and-swap (irreversibly sealing and invalidating other attempts on that batch), retry a stale attempt, abandon an attempt, and recycle a sealed batch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a batch has been sealed, no ward is still attempting to seal it, so its irreversible seal can never be applied a second time.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m1p5t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Targets

VARIABLES token, dropped, holdTarget, override
\* token: ring position holding exclusive-access token; dropped: targets already
\* hit by an irreversible retardant drop; holdTarget: target each drone has
\* locked in; override: whether the admin override is engaged.

vars == <<token, dropped, holdTarget, override>>

NumDrones == 3
Drones == 0..(NumDrones - 1)
None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Drones
    /\ dropped \subseteq Targets
    /\ holdTarget \in [Drones -> Targets \cup {None}]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ dropped = {}
    /\ holdTarget = [d \in Drones |-> None]
    /\ override = FALSE

\* The exclusive-access token rotates around the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % NumDrones
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, holdTarget, override>>

\* The token-holding drone locks in an unhit target no one else holds.
Lock(d, t) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ t \notin dropped
    /\ holdTarget[d] = None
    /\ \A e \in Drones : holdTarget[e] # t
    /\ holdTarget' = [holdTarget EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, dropped, override>>

\* The drone irreversibly drops on its locked target, retiring it: the target
\* is marked dropped and the lock is released together.
Drop(d) ==
    /\ holdTarget[d] # None
    /\ holdTarget[d] \notin dropped
    /\ dropped' = dropped \cup {holdTarget[d]}
    /\ holdTarget' = [holdTarget EXCEPT ![d] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, override>>

\* Under admin override, the operator forces a drop bypassing the token, but
\* still only on an unhit target, clearing any drone that had locked it.
AdminForceDrop(t) ==
    /\ override
    /\ t \notin dropped
    /\ dropped' = dropped \cup {t}
    /\ holdTarget' = [d \in Drones |-> IF holdTarget[d] = t THEN None ELSE holdTarget[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, override>>

\* The admin override is toggled.
ToggleOverride ==
    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, dropped, holdTarget>>

\* A hit target is cleared for a fresh surveillance pass.
Recycle(t) ==
    /\ t \in dropped
    /\ dropped' = dropped \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, holdTarget, override>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E d \in Drones, t \in Targets : Lock(d, t)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Drop(d)
    \/ \E t \in Targets : AdminForceDrop(t)
    \/ ToggleOverride
    \/ \E t \in Targets : Recycle(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A target that has been dropped on is locked by no drone, so its irreversible
\* retardant drop can never be issued a second time -- even under admin override.
AtMostOnce == \A t \in Targets : t \in dropped => \A d \in Drones : holdTarget[d] # t
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Targets = {f1, f2}
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm flies a ring of drones, and a single exclusive-access token circulates around the ring. Dropping fire retardant on a target is irreversible, so each target must be dropped on at most once. Only the drone currently holding the token may lock in a target, and it may lock only an unhit target that no other drone has already locked. The lock-holding drone then irreversibly drops on its target, retiring it: in one step the target is marked dropped and the lock is released. A privileged admin override lets a human operator force a drop while bypassing the token, but even the override may only drop on a still-unhit target, and forcing a drop clears any drone that had locked that target. The override can be toggled on and off. A hit target is eventually cleared for a fresh surveillance pass.

The actions are: rotate the token around the ring, the token-holder locks in an unhit unclaimed target, the lock-holder irreversibly drops (retiring the target), the admin forces a drop bypassing the token on an unhit target, toggle the admin override, and clear a hit target for reuse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A target that has been dropped on is locked by no drone, so its irreversible retardant drop can never be issued a second time, even under the admin override.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m6p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Registrars, Seats, CapLevels

VARIABLES lease, ttl, finalized, reqs, cap
\* lease: registrar leasing each seat; ttl: remaining lease ticks per seat;
\* finalized: seats irreversibly written to transcripts; reqs: pending lease
\* requests; cap: max concurrent leases, retuned at runtime.

vars == <<lease, ttl, finalized, reqs, cap>>

None == "none"
MaxTTL == 1
Reqs == [reg : Registrars, seat : Seats]
Leased == {s \in Seats : lease[s] # None}

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Seats -> Registrars \cup {None}]
    /\ ttl \in [Seats -> 0..MaxTTL]
    /\ finalized \subseteq Seats
    /\ reqs \subseteq Reqs
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ lease = [s \in Seats |-> None]
    /\ ttl = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
    /\ finalized = {}
    /\ reqs = {}
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* A registrar files a lease request for a seat.
Request(r, s) ==
    /\ [reg |-> r, seat |-> s] \notin reqs
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {[reg |-> r, seat |-> s]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, ttl, finalized, cap>>

\* A pending request is granted a fresh lease if the seat is free, not yet
\* finalized, and the concurrent-lease capacity has room.
Grant(m) ==
    /\ m \in reqs
    /\ lease[m.seat] = None
    /\ m.seat \notin finalized
    /\ Cardinality(Leased) < cap
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![m.seat] = m.reg]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![m.seat] = MaxTTL]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, cap>>

\* A lease's remaining time decays by one tick.
Decay(s) ==
    /\ lease[s] # None
    /\ ttl[s] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = ttl[s] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, finalized, reqs, cap>>

\* An expired lease (no time left) is reclaimed.
Expire(s) ==
    /\ lease[s] # None
    /\ ttl[s] = 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, finalized, reqs, cap>>

\* The lease-holder irreversibly writes the registration to the transcript,
\* retiring the seat: it is finalized and the lease is released in one step.
Finalize(r, s) ==
    /\ lease[s] = r
    /\ ttl[s] > 0
    /\ s \notin finalized
    /\ finalized' = finalized \cup {s}
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, reqs, cap>>

\* A finalized seat is reopened for a later term.
Reopen(s) ==
    /\ s \in finalized
    /\ finalized' = finalized \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, ttl, reqs, cap>>

\* The concurrent-lease capacity is retuned at runtime.
Recap ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels : cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, ttl, finalized, reqs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Seats : Request(r, s)
    \/ \E m \in reqs : Grant(m)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Decay(s)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Expire(s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Seats : Finalize(r, s)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Reopen(s)
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A seat whose registration has been finalized holds no lease and thus cannot
\* be finalized again, so the irreversible transcript write happens at most once.
AtMostOnce == \A s \in Seats : s \in finalized => lease[s] = None
=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system finalizes seat registrations onto student transcripts, an irreversible act that must happen at most once per seat. Seats are handed out with lease-based ownership with expiry, but leasing is two-phase: a registrar first files a lease request, and a pending request is granted a fresh lease only if the seat is free, not yet finalized, and the number of concurrent leases is below the current capacity. That capacity is retuned at runtime. Each granted lease carries a remaining-time counter that decays tick by tick; a lease with no time left is reclaimed. While its lease still has time, the lease-holder irreversibly writes the registration to the transcript, retiring the seat: the seat is finalized and the lease is released in the same step. A finalized seat is reopened only for a later term.

The actions are: file a lease request, grant a pending request within capacity, decay a lease's remaining time, reclaim an expired lease, irreversibly finalize a registration while the lease is valid (retiring the seat), reopen a finalized seat for a later term, and retune the concurrent-lease capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A seat whose registration has been finalized holds no lease and thus cannot be finalized again, so the irreversible transcript write happens at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m5p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, Players

VARIABLES waiting, playing, phase, candidates, votes
\* waiting: players in the matchmaking queue; playing: players currently in a
\* match; phase: idle/proposing; candidates: players proposed for the next
\* match; votes: each matchmaking server's ballot.

vars == <<waiting, playing, phase, candidates, votes>>

Quorum == 2
YesCount == Cardinality({s \in Servers : votes[s] = "yes"})

TypeOK ==
    /\ waiting \subseteq Players
    /\ playing \subseteq Players
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "proposing"}
    /\ candidates \subseteq Players
    /\ votes \in [Servers -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
    /\ waiting = Players
    /\ playing = {}
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ candidates = {}
    /\ votes = [s \in Servers |-> "none"]

\* Propose a two-player match drawn from the queue.
Propose(p, q) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ p # q
    /\ {p, q} \subseteq waiting
    /\ phase' = "proposing"
    /\ candidates' = {p, q}
    /\ votes' = [s \in Servers |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, playing>>

\* A matchmaking server approves the pairing.
VoteYes(s) ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ votes[s] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, playing, phase, candidates>>

\* A matchmaking server objects (skill mismatch).
VoteNo(s) ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ votes[s] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, playing, phase, candidates>>

\* With a quorum the match forms: candidates move from queue to match.
Form ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ YesCount >= Quorum
    /\ candidates \subseteq waiting
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ candidates
    /\ playing' = playing \cup candidates
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ candidates' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

\* The proposal is abandoned (no quorum among slow servers).
Abandon ==
    /\ phase = "proposing"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ candidates' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, playing, votes>>

\* A match ends: its players return to the queue.
EndMatch(p) ==
    /\ p \in playing
    /\ playing' = playing \ {p}
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, candidates, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p, q \in Players : Propose(p, q)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : VoteYes(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : VoteNo(s)
    \/ Form
    \/ Abandon
    \/ \E p \in Players : EndMatch(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Players are only ever moved between the queue and matches, never created or
\* lost, so the count in the queue plus the count in matches is always the
\* total roster size.
Conserved == Cardinality(waiting) + Cardinality(playing) = Cardinality(Players)
=============================================================================
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker sorts players between a matchmaking queue and active matches. Forming a match is authorized by quorum voting among the matchmaking servers: a two-player pairing is proposed from the queue, each server approves or objects, and the match forms only once a quorum of servers has approved. Servers may be slow but never fail, so a pairing that never gathers a quorum among slow servers is simply abandoned. When a match forms, exactly the proposed players move from the queue into the match; when a match ends, its players return to the queue. Players are only ever moved between the queue and matches -- none is created and none is lost -- so the roster is conserved.

The actions are: propose a two-player match from the queue, a server approves, a server objects, form the match once a quorum approves (moving the pair from queue to match), abandon a pairing that no quorum approved, and end a match (returning a player to the queue).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of players waiting in the queue plus the number of players in matches is always exactly the total roster size, since players are only moved and never created or lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m2p0t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances

VARIABLES owner, inCS, phase, votes, claimant
\* owner: instance holding the shared settlement gateway (or none); inCS: which
\* instances are in the critical section; phase: idle/voting for the grant 2PC;
\* votes: each participant's ballot; claimant: instance the grant is for.

vars == <<owner, inCS, phase, votes, claimant>>

None == "none"
AllYes == \A i \in Instances : votes[i] = "yes"
SomeNo == \E i \in Instances : votes[i] = "no"

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Instances \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ votes \in [Instances -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ claimant \in Instances \cup {None}

Init ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ inCS = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votes = [i \in Instances |-> "none"]
    /\ claimant = None

\* An instance opens a two-phase commit to be granted the gateway.
Request(i) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ owner = None
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ claimant' = i
    /\ votes' = [j \in Instances |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS>>

\* A participant votes to grant.
VoteYes(i) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[i] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, phase, claimant>>

\* A participant votes against (it wants the gateway itself).
VoteNo(i) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[i] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, phase, claimant>>

\* Unanimous grant makes the claimant the sole owner.
Grant ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ AllYes
    /\ owner = None
    /\ owner' = claimant
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ claimant' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, votes>>

\* Any objection denies the grant.
Deny ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ SomeNo
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ claimant' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, votes>>

\* Only the owner may enter the critical section.
Enter(i) ==
    /\ owner = i
    /\ ~inCS[i]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, phase, votes, claimant>>

\* Leave the critical section.
Exit(i) ==
    /\ inCS[i]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, phase, votes, claimant>>

\* Release the gateway once outside the critical section.
Release(i) ==
    /\ owner = i
    /\ ~inCS[i]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, phase, votes, claimant>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Request(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : VoteYes(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : VoteNo(i)
    \/ Grant
    \/ Deny
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Enter(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Exit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Release(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone in the critical section is the current gateway owner; since there is
\* a single owner, at most one instance is ever in the critical section.
MutualExclusion == \A i \in Instances : inCS[i] => owner = i
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2, i3}
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch runs on several independent processor instances that share one critical resource: a single settlement gateway that only one instance may use at a time. Access to the gateway is granted through a two-phase commit. An instance opens a grant vote for itself; each participant votes to grant or objects because it wants the gateway itself. A unanimous grant makes the requesting instance the sole owner of the gateway, while any objection denies the grant. Only the owner may enter the critical section, and it must leave the critical section before it can release the gateway back to the shared pool. Because there is only ever a single owner, no two instances can ever both be using the gateway at once.

The actions are: request a grant via two-phase commit, a participant votes to grant, a participant objects, grant the gateway to the claimant on a unanimous vote, deny the grant on any objection, the owner enters the critical section, an instance leaves the critical section, and the owner releases the gateway when outside the critical section.

CONSTANTS Instances

\* remaining lease ticks; inCS: which instances are in the critical section;
\* reqQ: instances waiting for the lease.

vars == <<owner, ttl, inCS, reqQ>>

MaxTTL == 2

    /\ ttl \in 0..MaxTTL
    /\ inCS \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ reqQ \subseteq Instances

    /\ owner = None
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ inCS = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

Request(i) ==
    /\ i \notin reqQ
    /\ reqQ' = reqQ \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, inCS>>

\* A free lease is granted to a waiting instance with a fresh term.
Grant(i) ==

    /\ i \in reqQ
    /\ owner' = i
    /\ ttl' = MaxTTL
    /\ reqQ' = reqQ \ {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED inCS

\* The lease term decays.
Decay ==
    /\ owner # None
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ ttl' = ttl - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, reqQ>>

\* An expired lease is released, but only once the owner has left the section.
Expire ==
    /\ owner # None
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ ~inCS[owner]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, inCS, reqQ>>

\* Only the lease owner, while its term is valid, may enter the section.
Enter(i) ==
    /\ owner = i
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ ~inCS[i]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, reqQ>>

\* Leave the critical section.
Exit(i) ==
    /\ inCS[i]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, reqQ>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Request(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Grant(i)
    \/ Decay
    \/ Expire
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Enter(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Exit(i)

\* has a single owner, at most one instance is ever in the section.
